#5256. Binance’s $6.3B Hack Fix Is Coming Tomorrow: Why the ZK Math Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot shows its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham says those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:

The striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, showed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:

Not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

What the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance says the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest update says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

A headline claiming that 1.8 billion XRP moved across the XRP Ledger within 24 hours has revived discussion of a network recovery. The figure hasn't been independently verified for a dated 24-hour period, so treat it as a reported claim, not confirmed evidence of a new trend.

The XRP Ledger handles payments, decentralized exchange transactions and tokenized assets. Payment volumes reflects the network activity, but the number needs context. Large transfers can be exchange custody movements, internal treasury operations or transfers between wallets controlled by the same entity.

None of that necessarily signals fresh investor demand or new capital entering the market.

Recent verified reporting shows why the distinction matters. One October snapshot had daily payment volume jumping to about 137.7 million XRP, still below its 30-day average of roughly 496 million.

Another October reading, around 363.3 million XRP, came with the same caution: a one-day rise did not establish a sustained recovery.

A reading near 1.8 billion XRP usually comes at the end of the week where most of the network activity occurs. The most likely outcome is always the same: high activity by Thursday and Friday and a tubmling on the weekend, with a recovery starting on Monday.

Other indicators help separate real adoption from a passing spike: active addresses, successful payment counts, decentralized-exchange trading, liquidity and how transaction sizes are distributed. Even high transaction counts can mislead when automated activity dominates, as recent investigations into small-value stablecoin payments on XRPL showed.

Network usage and XRP's market price are only indirectly related. More settlement activity doesn't guarantee higher token prices, and speculative buying can lift prices with no matching improvement in usage. Broader market conditions and exchange liquidity matter too.

A verified natural burst of XRP movement could mean renewed engagement with the network. A more convincing signal would be several consecutive days of stronger, widely distributed activity, backed by improving liquidity and sustained user demand, which rarely happens.

#5254. Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying, as Route 2 FI Buys the Dip

Bitcoin news: the Binance hacker holds $1.4B in BTC, 3x this week’s ETF inflows. Will Binance’s buyback help, and can BTC hold $76,500?

Bitcoin news on Friday turned to a warning from trader Route 2 FI, who said the Binance hacker’s $1.4 billion in BTC is more than three times what spot ETFs bought all week, a potential seller hanging over Bitcoin at $77,300.

Arkham’s entity page shows the Binance hacker holding 18,270 BTC worth $1.42 billion and 488,364 ETH worth $1.09 billion across 73 addresses. US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million from Monday to Thursday.

Route 2 FI still likes the setup enough to take a position. The trader expects Binance to recover fully but thinks the hack will push more people toward decentralized exchanges.

Binance would need a couple of months to fill this hole, unless they use other shady tactics to get whole faster.

The hacker has $BTC worth $1.4b and $ETH worth $1b ready to sell. For $BTC, that's more than 3x the $450M that spot ETFs bought all week.

— Route 2 FI (@Route2FI) October 30, 2026

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Route 2 FI’s math holds up. Arkham’s Binance Hacker entity shows 18,270 BTC, worth $1.42 billion at Friday’s prices. SoSoValue figures show US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million across four straight days of inflows from October 26 to 29. That makes the hacker’s Bitcoin about 3.2 times a week of ETF demand.

Binance hacker holdings on October 30, 2026 vs spot Bitcoin ETF inflows for October 26 to 29. Sources: Arkham, SoSoValue.

The hacker hasn’t sold any of the Bitcoin yet. The selling so far has been in smaller tokens: Lookonchain tracked the attacker dumping UNI, PEPE, ENA, LINK and others for 70,480 ETH, worth about $158 million.

On the other side, Binance is already buying. The exchange told CoinDesk it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses, $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens the attackers took, and is buying the rest on exchanges and over the counter. About $3 billion of the stolen funds is frozen and doesn’t need replacing.

“Binance’s SAFU fund and Binance’s holdings include a large amount of assets such as BTC and ETH. We are currently buying, through OTC and on-exchange, all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts.”

That matters for Bitcoin. If Binance already holds enough BTC to cover customers, its buying lands mostly on altcoins, which leaves the hacker’s 18,270 BTC as a seller without a matching buyer.

Route 2 FI pointed to the Bybit hack as the template. Attackers took about $1.4 billion in ether from Bybit on February 21, 2025, and the exchange replaced it within days through loans, deposits and market purchases.

The buyback gave prices only a short lift. Measured from the February 20, 2025 close on Binance:

Ethereum bounced while Bybit bought, then lost more than a third of its value within three weeks. The broader market sold off over that stretch for reasons beyond the hack, so the table shows that buyback demand fades fast. It doesn’t show that the hack caused the slide.

Route 2 FI also argued that the hack, coming a year after the October 10, 2025 crash, gives traders another reason to keep less money on centralized exchanges. Binance paid out more than $283 million in compensation after that crash, when some assets lost their pegs on its platform.

The trader cited the jump in Hyperliquid’s HYPE token as proof. The timing doesn’t fit, though. HYPE rose from $79.38 to a $97.09 high between 10:00 and 16:00 UTC on Thursday, after ICE and Trade.xyz announced plans for a regulated US perpetuals venue on Hyperliquid. That was about ten hours before the Binance drain began at 20:04 UTC.

After the hack, HYPE fell to $88.55 and trades at $90.83.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Whale Sends $35M to Coinbase at a $15M Loss as October Turns Red: What Moves BTC Next?

The setup Route 2 FI is buying is easy to see on the daily chart since early August. Bitcoin’s $76,500 low on Friday stopped $35 above its 200-day EMA at $76,465, a line it has closed above every day since the late-August breakout. BTC trades at $77,326, down 3.5% in 24 hours.

August 2 to October 30, 2026: BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

The last time Bitcoin tested the 200-day line, in mid-September, it held at $74,968 and climbed to $87,395 within a week. A trader buying here has a clear line to be wrong at.

For Bitcoin news over the coming week, two things decide which row plays out: whether Binance reopens withdrawals on schedule, and whether the hacker’s Bitcoin starts to move.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. In late October 2026, Zcash (ZEC) reached a key milestone: the coin's price consolidated around $1,280, and its market capitalization hit $21.8 billion. However, the rapid rally was overshadowed by a sharp split within the community.

The trigger of the crisis was not a technical problem but a revolt of large investors over the targeted spending of capital.

Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), the organization that distributes part of the miners' block reward, launched the Zcash Adoption Pool program. The fund directed grants toward the integration of vulnerable groups like refugees without access to banks.

The decision sparked protest from major players, since ZCG's charter allows it to distribute multimillion-dollar budgets bypassing the coinholder vote. The "whale" revolt moved into the practical realm: a major holder under the pseudonym "big z" publicly announced a full sell-off of his ZEC holdings.

According to him, the fund should finance cryptography, not political manifestos.

The local conflict quickly grew into a debate about the nature of decentralized money, which industry heavyweights joined. Developer Sean Bowe published a manifesto on the future of ZCG, in which he called for revising the fund's financing due to the anomalous surge in the ZEC price.

The initiative was unexpectedly supported by legendary investor Naval Ravikant, who laconically snapped that a $50 million cap is more than enough for community grants.

Meanwhile, the fund's activists continue to insist that private money is a "humanitarian imperative" and a public good.

However, Gemini exchange co-founder Tyler Winklevoss harshly challenged this thesis: a commercial network with transaction fees cannot be a public good. Winklevoss compared ZCG's actions to "taxation without representation" and called for leaving the development of Zcash to the free market.

The pressure on the price from the whales' coin sell-off coincided with the launch of direct ZEC deposits on the decentralized Rujira Network on October 29.

After failing to break above $1,390, the price settled in the $1,220–1,245 $range, still well below the all-time high of $1,698 set in late September. The fundamental dispute over who should control Zcash's millions remains open.

According to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, the Binance hacker has dumped more than 130 altcoins across EVM chains, generating about $279 million in proceeds.

A security incident at digital asset exchange Binance last Thursday affected some $6.3 billion in assets, making it the largest crypto theft on record. Binance's initial investigation suggested the security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

How many altcoins has the Binance hacker dumped? On EVM chains alone, the hacker dumped over 130 altcoins, receiving: 123,400 $ETH ($277.26M) 1.69M $USDC Total: $279M https://t.co/Y8JYpWRP73

In a recent analysis on X, Lookonchain examined how many altcoins the Binance hacker has dumped. It noted that on EVM chains alone, the hacker dumped over 130 altcoins, sharing the list of some tokens affected in a table including SHIB. The hacker dumped 499,926,072,560 SHIB with a selling value of 873 ETH worth $1,960,615.

In return for the altcoins sold, the hacker received 123,400 ETH worth $277.26 million and 1.69 million USDC, totaling approximately $279 million.

The Binance hacker continues to swap stolen funds. In a recent report by Lookonchain, the hacker is swapping the stolen 970,522 SOL worth $95.9 million for BTC.

As reported, the over 499 billion SHIB stolen in the Binance hack represented 0.05% of its supply, with the SHIB price relatively absorbing the selloff.

Shiba Inu price saw a sharp selloff on October 29, alongside the rest of the crypto market in an initial reaction to the news of the Binance hack. The drop hit a low of $0.00000446 on Friday, from where SHIB sharply rebounded. Shiba Inu closed Saturday in the red, marking a loss of 18.92% in October.

Shiba Inu rebounded thereafter, fluctuating between $0.00000466 and $0.00000472 on November's first day as the price awaits further direction. At the time of writing, SHIB was down 0.04% in the last 24 hours to $0.00000469 and down 3.14% weekly.

Binance says it has replenished about 95% of the impacted assets, reiterating a clear commitment to absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds. The crypto exchange also said it will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens.

October ended for XRP with a drop of almost 19%. The main blow was the $6.3 billion hack of the Binance exchange, which dragged down the entire market. However, the sell-off recorded at the lows activated large buy orders — the current liquidity map points to the formation of local support.

Now the XRP price is squeezed in a narrow corridor around $1.25, testing the boundaries of the local bottom.

CoinGlass derivatives market data shows that the asset has literally been pinned to the floor. At the current rate of $1.2505, the critical level of long liquidations is at the $1.2292 mark. The probability of its test within 24 hours is 54%. From above, the price is held back by a block of short sellers at the $1.4292 level.

At the same time, the market has already been cleared of excessive leverage — $37.6 million in longs were forcibly closed in October.

The TradingView technical picture confirms the importance of the current line. On the weekly chart, XRP is trading right on the key 200-week moving average ($1.25–$1.28) — this is a powerful historical level from which the vertical takeoff began in August. The daily oscillator dropped to the 36.85 mark.

Historically, reaching this oversold zone has always preceded an upward trend reversal.

Additional pressure was exerted by the results of the Ripple Swell conference. The new RLUSD stablecoin takes over the company’s institutional products (including custodial services for Coinbase and Robinhood), which temporarily reduced direct demand for XRP.

Against this background, the assets of U.S. XRP ETFs corrected to $1.42–$1.47 billion solely due to the drop in the price of the token itself, while inflows into the funds froze near zero.

The $1.20–$1.25 range remains the main foundation. The fact that the dump on the Binance news was instantly bought back proves the strength of buyers. If they hold the $1.2292 line and return the price above the daily average at $1.3145, the current marks will become the official bottom.

Conversely, a breakdown of $1.20 will open the way to the August lows around $0.98–$1.00.

XRP recorded 7,934 new wallets, while payment volume reportedly surged to 1.33 billion XRP, signalling increased network activity.

Ripple's institutional developments and expanding XRPL ecosystem strengthen the long-term adoption narrative, although direct XRP demand remains uncertain.

XRP must defend the $1.23 to $1.26 support zone and reclaim resistance to confirm a potential recovery, with $1.50 remaining a key upside hurdle.

XRP price is trading near $1.25, with its price struggling to regain bullish momentum despite growing activity across the XRP Ledger. The latest Binance security breach, involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen assets, has added another layer of uncertainty to the market, triggering significant customer outflows from the exchange.

However, Binance has since reported that XRP is among the assets fully backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio under its latest Proof of Reserves verification. While this offers some reassurance to customers, it does not necessarily signal fresh buying demand for XRP. Meanwhile, network activity is picking up, raising an important question:

Could the surge in XRP adoption support a price recovery, or will bearish technical conditions continue to weigh on the token?

While XRP’s price continues to hover near $1.25, activity across the XRP Ledger is showing encouraging signs of growth. Recent on-chain data points to an increase in wallet creation and payment activity, adding to the broader adoption narrative.

The XRP Ledger recorded 7,934 new wallets on November 1, marking its sixth-largest daily increase of 2026, according to Santiment. The figure was more than double the recent 30-day average of approximately 3,500 new accounts. The increase is particularly notable, as it occurred on a Sunday, typically a quieter day for crypto network activity.

As per data from XRPScan, XRP’s reported payment volume climbed from approximately 229 million to 1.33 billion XRP within 24 hours. This points to a significant increase in transaction activity across the network. However, the surge needs further examination to determine whether it reflects organic payment adoption, large wallet transfers or exchange-related movements.

Ripple’s regulatory progress, banking relationships and developments around institutional custody are adding to the longer-term adoption outlook. Meanwhile, the broader tokenization push and XRPL’s expanding DeFi ecosystem could create additional use cases for the network. However, these developments do not automatically translate into direct buying demand for XRP.

Taken together, these developments suggest that XRP’s network activity is improving even as its price struggles to gain momentum.

XRP is attempting to stabilise around $1.25 after an extended decline from its 2025 highs. The weekly chart shows that the token has recently struggled to sustain its recovery above the $1.50 to $1.60 resistance zone, with sellers pushing prices back towards the immediate support area of $1.23 to $1.26. This region represents the immediate support zone on the shared weekly chart. XRP needs to sustain this area to prevent another move towards the lower levels.

The weekly chart suggests the XRP price is hitting the middle bands of Bollinger, and a rebound is much expected from here to prevent an extended bearish move. On the other hand, the weekly MACD shows a drop in bullish pressure, with the levels heading towards a bearish crossover.

Bullish scenario: XRP holds the $1.23 to $1.23 support zone. Sustained buying pressure could open the way towards $1.50 to $1.60. A breakout above this resistance zone would strengthen the recovery outlook.

Bearish scenario: A sustained weekly breakdown below $1.23 could expose the $0.9947 support level. Failure to defend this region would further weaken the recovery structure.

XRP’s improving network activity and institutional developments offer encouraging signs for its longer-term adoption outlook. The addition of 7,934 new wallets and the reported surge in payment volume suggest that activity across the XRP Ledger is picking up, even as the token struggles to regain bullish momentum.

However, the price action has yet to reflect these developments convincingly. XRP needs to defend the $1.25 support region and reclaim nearby resistance before it can establish a stronger recovery. A move towards $1.50 would provide a more meaningful sign of improving market structure.

For now, the fundamental picture is constructive, but the technical outlook remains cautious. Whether growing network participation can translate into sustained buying pressure will be crucial in determining XRP’s next major move.

The volume of tokenized stocks on the Ethereum network grew by 170% over the year, reaching $827 million by the end of October 2026. According to a fresh report from the analytics platform Token Terminal, the real-world assets (RWA) sector has outgrown the experimental stage.

While the total value of tokenized securities on alternative chains is measured in billions of dollars, the volume on Ethereum remains in the range from $827 million to $841 million, and the network remains one of the key channels for digitized equities.

The rapid growth of the sector is largely tied to how the digital assets themselves are structured. At the moment, 86% of tokenized stocks are issued under the model of classic stablecoins: the instruments are fully backed by the underlying asset in a 1:1 ratio and, at the same time, function without the direct operational or legal participation of the issuer of the original securities.

Ethereum, which currently controls 53.8% of the global stablecoin market ($158.71 billion out of a total of $294.75 billion), carries its well-tested and liquid infrastructure over to traditional securities.

Professional market participants assess this shift as a potential repetition of the success of stablecoins, but this time in the stock market.

While spot infrastructure is being built on Ethereum, a completely different, speculative life is unfolding in the derivatives market. Here, historical records are being set on decentralized venues: open interest, with contracts on the same tokenized stocks accounting for the largest share, has reached $1.76 billion.

An example of this ecosystem is the Hyperliquid platform, whose native token HYPE is trading at around $87.70. The coin is supported by an inflow of new holders, as well as automated tokenomics: the platform directs $1.24 million daily to buying back HYPE from the open market.

Representatives of the investment community have outlined the zone from $70 to $76 as a key long-term support level. Current market conditions point to a possible move toward the $90–$100 range.

The existence of this parallel reality — from spot on Ethereum to highly liquid futures on Hyperliquid — shows that the blockchain is becoming a multi-level environment for different types of capital.

#5240. Why Coinbase Bitcoin Discount Just Hit a Yearly High

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Classic crypto market metrics have suddenly stopped reflecting reality. Bitcoin’s discount on the U.S. exchange Coinbase relative to the international Binance has hit a yearly high, with the Coinbase Premium Index collapsing to around −0.06%.

In normal times, such a chart gives traders a cold sweat: the index going deep into the red zone means that large funds in the U.S. have started massively dumping crypto.

However, the current collapse of the indicator turned out to be a technical illusion. It was provoked by the emergency freeze of operations on Binance immediately after a large-scale hack of the exchange, which completely blocked classic cross-exchange arbitrage.

The anomalous price gap coincided with the largest incident in the industry’s history: on October 29–30, hackers attacked Binance’s hot wallets, withdrawing about $6.3 billion. The exchange promptly froze half of the stolen funds on the blockchain, and the head of the platform promised to fully cover the remaining client losses from the SAFU reserve fund.

Nevertheless, amid the panic, the price of Bitcoin dropped to $77,000–$78,000.

To localize the problem, Binance completely shut the gateways — it temporarily banned any deposits and withdrawals of funds. This decision instantly paralyzed cross-exchange arbitrage. Large players physically could not buy the temporarily cheaper Bitcoin on Coinbase and transfer it to Binance to even out the price.

Liquidity was locked inside the platforms, which caused the discount to artificially swell to its widest level in a year.

As noted by Galaxy Research’s head of research Alex Thorn, due to the blocking of transactions, the discount on Coinbase temporarily stopped being a signal of weak demand in the U.S.

On November 1, Binance announced a phased reopening of withdrawals, starting with BTC and ETH. Now the market is waiting to see how quickly arbitrageurs eliminate the gap. If the gap closes in the coming days, it means the anomaly was purely technical.

If the negative spread becomes entrenched, it will be an alarming signal of a real cooling of American capital.

#5239. BTCPay Server Tells Merchants to Shut Down After Attackers Sweep Hot Wallets: Are Payments Still Safe?

Bitcoin news: BTCPay Server told merchants to go offline after attackers swept hot wallets on 2.4.1 or older. Here is who is exposed.

In today’s Bitcoin news, BTCPay Server, the free open-source payment processor many Bitcoin merchants run themselves, told every operator to shut down their instance after reports that attackers were sweeping the hot wallets on merchant servers. Less than six hours later, the culprit was old software.

At 04:07 UTC on Monday, the project said its investigation had found an attack vector aimed at servers running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. It has “no credible reports” of drains on the current 2.4.7. BTCPay has not said how much was stolen or how many stores were hit.

That makes this a different kind of Bitcoin news from last week’s Binance hack. No exchange was breached. Merchants who run their own payment stack, the people self-custody is meant to protect, were the target.

So who was exposed, and what should store owners do now?

Unauthorized attackers are reportedly draining hot wallets on @BtcpayServer instances.

Users running BTCPay Server instances are advised to shut them down immediately. pic.twitter.com/H7mXfJLLcD

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 2, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

An attacker logged in as admin on older servers and emptied the hot wallets. BTCPay Server raised the alarm at 22:25 UTC on Sunday and asked operators to run its shutdown script “until we complete the investigation.”

Two hours later, founder Nicolas Dorier said the project’s own public servers on 2.4.7 were not attacked. “The attacker managed to log in as admin on those instance, we are still trying to figure out how,” he wrote.

📢 Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older.

We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server… pic.twitter.com/gYxK4Bb7fc

— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 2, 2026

A hot wallet keeps its signing keys on the server itself, so it can pay out refunds and payouts automatically. Anyone with admin rights on that server can send the coins too.

Hosting providers moved fast. BTCPay thanked LunaNode and others for shutting down older hosted instances on their own, so some merchants may find their store offline on Monday.

The version history is the story. 2.4.1 shipped on July 23. Two weeks later, 2.4.2 fixed a critical flaw the team said was “being actively exploited,” and five more releases followed, ending with Thursday’s 2.4.7, which fixed 85 findings from an AI security scan Anthropic ran for the project.

Whether this is the same hole as August’s is still open. Dorier said a blog post with more detail is coming.

Only if it still runs 2.4.1 or older, on what the project knows so far. “For those who already updated at least once since the release of 2.4.2, there is no reason to panic,” Dorier wrote at 04:10 UTC.

The reported drains all hit hot wallets. Stores that receive into a watch-only wallet keep their signing keys off the server altogether.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

No. BTC sat at $77,890 when the alert went out and traded at $78,102 on Binance at 07:40 UTC on Monday, up 0.3% in a day. The market is still chewing on last week’s Binance hack.

That hack set the floor. Bitcoin fell to $76,326 on October 30, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average), now at $76,512, and buyers have held above it for three days. Above, the 50-day EMA at $80,293 is now overhead, and $81,971, the October 29 high before the hack, caps the range.

The Fear & Greed Index reads 37, fear, and BTC is down 2.5% on the week.

#5236. Nvidia, Nike and 48 Other Companies Oppose OKX Stock Tokenization Plan

A total of 50 companies, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE), have officially raised objections to the trading of tokenized shares on a new platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

As per the most recent public notice by the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), OKXICE, the total number of companies objecting to the initiative has reached 50 as of Oct. 30.

The total increased from 38 companies on Oct. 28, with 12 additional companies raising objections in just two days.

The new names that recently raised objections include Nvidia, Nike, Costco (COST), Micron Technology (MU) and Reddit (RDDT).

Other companies that have recently raised objections include cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), Bloom Energy (BE), IREN (IREN), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Big names in the financial world, including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC), have also raised objections.

Some other prominent names include Walmart (WMT), Coca-Cola (KO), McDonald's (MCD), Eli Lilly (LLY), Adobe (ADBE) and Dell Technologies (DELL).

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Each of them owns a 50% stake in the joint venture.

The goal is to enable tokenized versions of traditional US stocks to be traded on the blockchain.

Instead of buying these shares on a traditional brokerage platform, eligible investors can trade blockchain tokens that represent ownership interests in the underlying securities.

The platform will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, as per the company's public notice.

The planned platform will be based on a temporary regulatory exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Sept. 17.

However, the regulator gave companies the option to object to any unauthorized third-party tokenization of their shares.

If a company submits an objection within the specified timeframe, then its third-party tokenized shares cannot be offered by the platform under the exemption.

#5234. Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials

The HKMA plans to bring regulated stablecoins into tokenized government debt trials, while HSBC says its RedCoin stablecoin has reached 50,000 users.

Hong Kong has expanded its Project Ensemble pilot to allow round-the-clock settlement of tokenized transactions, as the city’s monetary regulator prepares to bring regulated stablecoins into trials involving tokenized government debt.

On Monday, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said that it had advanced its EnsembleTX project to a new stage allowing 24/7 real-value transactions. The HKMA said the update would help banks and their clients move funds globally, manage tokenized investments and handle treasury operations outside conventional settlement hours.

Participating banks initially settled payments through Hong Kong’s existing dollar settlement system, which limited settlement hours. When the pilot began real-value trials in November 2025, the HKMA said it planned to introduce tokenized central bank money to allow settlement around the clock.

The HKMA launched Project Ensemble in March 2024 to explore how banks could settle tokenized transactions using wholesale central bank digital money. A sandbox opened that August, allowing banks to connect their tokenized deposit platforms and test transactions.

Speaking at Hong Kong FinTech Week on Monday, HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said the regulator was introducing tokenized central bank money as a “foundation layer” for 24/7 settlement. He said tokenized bonds, money market funds and bank deposits were already being used.

The HKMA also said recognized dealers had completed secondary-market trial trades in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, a form of short-term debt issued by the regulator. It plans to expand those trials to include regulated stablecoins.

Separately, HSBC Group CEO Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong FinTech Week that the bank’s recently launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin, had reached 50,000 users about 10 days after its debut.

“We have 50,000 users,” Elhedery said, adding that HSBC was targeting “multi-million users” as it expands access to the token.

RedCoin’s rollout brings stablecoins to retail payments, while Ensemble’s settlement work has focused on transactions involving banks and tokenized investments.

Elhedery said HSBC was also offering tokenized deposits to wholesale clients in Hong Kong and about half a dozen other jurisdictions, allowing funds to move around the clock.

Related: Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push

The bank launched RedCoin on Oct. 23 for transfers and merchant payments through its PayMe application. HSBC said more than 3.3 million PayMe customers could activate stablecoin wallets to use the token. It also plans to bring the stablecoin into its mobile banking app and allow subscriptions to tokenized investments, including a Hong Kong dollar money market fund share class.

HSBC was among Hong Kong’s first licensed stablecoin issuers in April alongside Anchorpoint Financial, a venture backed by Animoca Brands and Standard Chartered. The city’s licensing regime, introduced in August 2025, requires issuers to meet standards for backing reserves, redemption and risk management.

Chainlink is trading at about $11.61, well off its late-September peak near $15.75. On the daily chart, what was a strong bullish run has turned into a corrective consolidation, and right now the price is testing support.

LINK's bullish reversal came in August. It broke above its major moving averages and ran from roughly $8.00 to $15.75. The decline that followed has carved out lower highs and lower lows, and short-term momentum has deteriorated along the way.

The price is now under the shorter-term moving averages, which are bunched around $12.00–$12.60, so sellers still control the near-term trend. Still, LINK is holding above its 200-day moving average near $11.00, and as long as it does, the wider recovery stays intact.

The first support is $11.40–$11.50. Below that sits $11.00, a psychological level. If that gives way for good, the $10.40–$10.60 region comes into view; buyers showed up there recently.

Resistance starts near $12.00–$12.20, and the $12.50–$12.70 supply zone above it is the stronger barrier. Win those back, and a recovery toward $13.30 starts to look more likely.

Daily RSI is around 40–45, on the weak side of neutral. Buying momentum is subdued, but LINK isn't deeply oversold.

There was a sharp wick down toward $10.30 recently, and the price climbed back above $11.50 afterward. That could mean demand is soaking up the selling. One rejection candle doesn't confirm a reversal, though.

Short term, LINK looks neutral to bearish. Its next real move will probably be decided by the $11.00 support and the $12.20–$12.70 resistance zone.

NEAR Protocol trades near $4.40. It had a big rally off its August range of $1.60–$1.80, and even after the latest pullback the bigger structure still looks healthy. Short-term momentum is fading, though, so it may need to consolidate for a while before the next sustained leg up.

The breakout came in September. NEAR tore through several resistance levels and topped out around $6.00 in early October, on much heavier volume than usual, a sign that a lot of the market was taking part.

Since that peak it's been correcting: lower highs, and one test after another of the $4.20–$4.40 support region.

Right now NEAR is trading under its short-term moving averages, with resistance around $4.50–$4.80. The intermediate and long-term averages are still rising and sit well below the price, so the broader bullish structure doesn't look broken yet.

First support is $4.20–$4.30, the area that kept getting tested during the recent consolidation.

Under that, $4.00 is both a psychological and a technical support level. A decisive break there could expose $3.60–$3.70, roughly where the rising longer-period moving average sits.

On the upside, the first resistance is around $4.55–$4.70, then $4.90–$5.00. Break above $5.00 and hold, and the way could open toward $5.40, eventually $5.80–$6.00.

Volume exploded during the September breakout, so there was real buying behind it. It has cooled off since, as the price consolidates, and that points to less speculative interest.

The daily RSI has dropped back to around 40–45. Momentum is weaker, but there's no clear oversold signal. The latest bounce from roughly $4.00 shows buyers are still active lower down. It needs stronger follow-through to count for much. Getting back above $4.70, then $5.00, could restart the upward momentum, with $5.40–$5.80 as the target.

NEAR's longer-term chart still looks healthy, but the short term is under corrective pressure. It has to hold $4.00–$4.20. A recovery to $4.70–$5.00 would be stronger evidence that buyers are taking back control.

BNB broke out hard in late August and climbed from about $600 to $800. October was a different story, with a run of lower highs as buying pressure faded. The latest decline knocked BNB under its short-term moving averages at $730–$750, which tilts the near-term picture bearish.

On the way down, $700 is the first support, and $690 is the next. A confirmed daily close below $690 could speed up selling toward $670–$650.

The daily RSI is around 40–45. Momentum has weakened, but it isn't at extreme oversold levels, so a technical bounce is still possible. It would need stronger confirmation, though.

Bitcoin is trading near $77,871 after a sharp correction from its October peak around $87,000. Short-term momentum on the daily chart is getting worse, and BTC is closing in on a support zone that could decide where it goes next.

The August reversal was a strong one. BTC broke above its major moving averages and rallied from roughly $63,000 to $87,000. Then October brought a string of lower highs, as demand weakened and selling pressure built.

The latest drop took BTC below its short-term moving averages, which are concentrated around $80,500–$82,000. That area is now heavy overhead resistance.

The price recently dipped to about $76,000 before recovering toward $77,900. The rising 200-day moving average runs through the $76,000–$77,000 area, and another intermediate-term average is close by, so support is stacked there.

Immediate resistance is around $78,500–$79,000, then $80,500–$82,000. A sustained breakout above $82,000 would strengthen the case for a recovery and could bring $84,000–$86,000 into reach.

If BTC loses $76,000, the broader bullish structure weakens and a correction toward $74,000–$72,000 becomes more likely.

Daily RSI has dropped to about 40. That's bearish momentum, but it's getting near the levels where short relief rallies can start.

Selling volume has been high lately, so plenty of traders took part in the decline. That's why any return of buying demand needs to be confirmed.

Holding $76,000–$77,000 and taking back $80,500 could set off a recovery toward $82,000–$84,000.

A confirmed breakdown below $76,000 could speed up selling toward $74,000, possibly $72,000.

Bitcoin is testing a major long-term support region, and the short-term outlook is cautiously bearish. Defending $76,000 is what keeps the broader recovery intact. Reclaiming $82,000 would be a clearer sign that bullish momentum is back.

A four-hour close above $1.27 could strengthen the bullish outlook, while a break below $1.23 may invite further selling.

A 50 million XRP withdrawal worth approximately $62.4 million from Binance has added to market interest.

XRP is approaching a critical setup as volatility contracts and traders prepare for a potential breakout. The token’s four-hour Bollinger Bands have narrowed to levels last seen in August, a pattern that previously preceded a sharp price rally. With the XRP price approaching a key decision zone, two levels could determine whether XRP stages a recovery or faces another decline.

XRP’s four-hour Bollinger Bands have compressed to their narrowest levels since August, according to crypto analyst Ali Charts. The analyst noted that the previous time the bands reached a similar level of compression, XRP rallied 71% within three days. This has renewed attention on the possibility of another significant price move.

However, a Bollinger Bands squeeze indicates declining volatility rather than a confirmed bullish breakout. The price can move sharply in either direction once volatility expands.

Ali Charts has identified two levels that could determine XRP’s next direction:

Until either level breaks, the analyst considers the $1.23–$1.27 range a no-trade zone.

Whale activity has added another development to XRP’s market outlook. According to transaction data, an unidentified whale withdrew 50 million XRP from Binance. The transfer was valued at approximately $62.4 million at the time. Large exchange withdrawals can indicate that investors are moving tokens into private wallets rather than keeping them readily available for trading.

Still, the transfer has drawn attention as XRP approaches its key technical levels.

XRP’s four-hour chart shows the token trading within a narrowing range after an extended decline. The Bollinger Bands compression suggests that the current consolidation could soon give way to a larger price move. The immediate resistance stands at $1.27. A confirmed four-hour close above this level could improve buying momentum and bring $1.30 into focus.

On the downside, $1.23 remains the key support. A break below this level could expose XRP to further selling pressure and weaken the recovery outlook. For now, neither direction has been confirmed. A decisive candle close beyond the $1.23–$1.27 range, supported by stronger trading volume, would provide a clearer indication of the next trend.

XRP’s tightening Bollinger Bands and the latest whale withdrawal have put the token at an important technical juncture. However, the previous 71% rally following a similar setup does not guarantee another sharp rise.

A break above $1.27 could strengthen the bullish case, while a move below $1.23 would put sellers in control. Until then, XRP remains in a consolidation phase, with its next major move dependent on which level gives way first.

#5229. 40 Million XRP Moved From Binance Hacker Wallet

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert has reported that a wallet linked to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack has just sent 40 million XRP (~$50.5 million) to a mystery address.

On Nov. 2, Whale Alert shared information about the huge XRP transfer, noting that the transaction initiator is an address tagged "Binance Hack 2026."

The huge transfer took place at 03:56 UTC, Whale Alert data shows. The transaction involved 40 million XRP (~$50.46 million).

Interestingly, just 50 seconds before that, Whale Alert reported another transfer of 40 million XRP.

Another 40 million XRP (~$50.44 million) was also sent from the wallet tagged as "Binance Hack 2026" to a mystery address.

In total, these two transfers involved 80 million XRP (~$100.9 million).

Both transfers originated from the same wallet but were sent to separate mystery addresses.

It is still unclear why these transfers were made. There is no sign that these funds have been sent to a crypto exchange or sold yet.

The transactions took place just days after Binance faced one of the biggest cryptocurrency hacks ever.

The massive XRP transfers came shortly after Binance started to restore cryptocurrency withdrawals following the unprecedented security breach the cryptocurrency exchange faced.

On Nov. 1, Binance annonced that the exchange would restore withdrawals in phases for 15 blockchain networks, including XRP Ledger, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana.

It also mentioned that withdrawals would be gradually restored for other networks, such as Tron, Dogecoin, Zcash, Avalanche, Sui, Polygon and Arbitrum.

The first stage of withdrawal resumption was set to take place between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on Nov. 1.

After Binance faced a security breach on Oct. 29, which led to the loss of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from its hot wallets, it temporarily paused withdrawals.

The exchange noted that withdrawals would be restored gradually after the security and infrastructure checks had been performed.

Binance also said that XRP balances were already fully backed, as were those of other major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and BNB.

Binance claimed that, as of Nov. 1, around 95% of affected assets had been replenished. The remaining 5% consists primarily of less liquid cryptocurrencies.

Cryptocurrency investors frequently ask how to cash out Bitcoin and convert their digital assets into traditional currency. Multiple pathways exist to transform bitcoin into cash or bank deposits, each with distinct advantages and processing times.

The question of can you cash out bitcoins for real money has a straightforward answer: yes, through several established channels. Each method comes with distinct fee structures and processing times that users should evaluate based on their specific needs.

Crypto exchanges represent the most common method for converting bitcoin to fiat currency. These platforms allow users to sell bitcoin at current market rates and withdraw funds directly to linked bank accounts. Processing times typically range from one to five business days.

Peer-to-peer platforms connect bitcoin sellers directly with buyers, eliminating intermediary involvement. These services offer greater flexibility in payment methods including bank transfers, cash deposits, or digital payment services. Users should verify buyer credentials to avoid potential fraud.

Bitcoin ATMs provide immediate cash conversion for those wondering how do i cash in bitcoins quickly. These machines allow users to sell bitcoin and receive physical currency on the spot. While convenient, bitcoin ATMs typically charge higher fees ranging from 7% to 15% per transaction.

The process of converting bitcoin to cash follows a consistent framework regardless of the chosen method.

Cashing out Bitcoin through crypto exchange services may trigger capital gains tax obligations, depending on local regulations. Keeping accurate transaction records helps ensure proper tax reporting.

Crypto exchange services must also comply with Know Your Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) requirements. Identity verification and additional compliance checks may affect processing times, particularly for larger transactions.

Security remains paramount when converting cryptocurrency to cash. Users should implement several protective measures:

Transaction fees significantly impact the net amount received when converting bitcoin to cash. Exchange fees typically include trading fees, withdrawal fees, and network fees for blockchain transactions. Understanding these costs helps users maximize their returns.

Market volatility affects bitcoin prices, and strategic timing can result in better exchange rates. Some platforms offer reduced fees for higher trading volumes.

Some merchants now accept bitcoin directly as payment, eliminating the need for conversion. This approach allows holders to use their bitcoin while avoiding transaction fees associated with converting to fiat currency.

Bitcoin debit cards automatically convert cryptocurrency to fiat currency at the point of sale. These cards function like traditional debit cards but draw funds from bitcoin balances.

Converting bitcoin to cash involves navigating multiple platforms, methods, and considerations. Success requires understanding fee structures, security practices, and regulatory requirements while balancing speed against cost. Whether someone needs immediate cash through ATMs or prefers the economy of exchange transfers, options exist for various priorities. The key to answering can you cash out bitcoins for real money lies in selecting appropriate methods aligned with individual needs and maintaining security awareness.

#5226. Hackers Use Claude, Gemini and Kimi to Identify Valuable Crypto Targets

Cybercriminals are using popular artificial intelligence (AI) models like Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Moonshot AI's Kimi AI to evaluate the financial worth of potential victims, including those owning cryptocurrencies.

Cybersecurity researchers at Cisco Talos detailed in a new report how a new type of Windows malware dubbed VOLTA-AUTODOXER, or simply VOLTA, steals sensitive data and uses AI tools to identify potentially lucrative targets among compromised users.

Compared to traditional information-stealing malware, which mainly steals passwords and credentials, VOLTA can also analyze stolen data to build victim profiles and determine what assets hackers can potentially exploit for profit.

Notably, one of VOLTA's most dangerous features is its ability to extract sensitive crypto wallet information, including recovery seed phrases, which can potentially give attackers access to digital assets.

VOLTA also includes features that can crack cryptocurrency wallet vaults, posing a big risk for people who store their crypto wallet credentials on their computers.

But its features are not just limited to stealing crypto.

As explained by Cisco Talos security researcher Ryan Fetterman, VOLTA can also grab saved browser passwords, payment card info, authentication tokens, email credentials and active sessions on popular platforms like Telegram, Discord, Steam and Roblox.

It can also extract info from Outlook accounts and Slack workspaces, as well as other personal and professional information on the infected system.

The malware also takes things further by analyzing victims' email accounts to grab more personal data.

For example, it can scan Gmail accounts for purchase confirmations and receipts from services like Amazon, PayPal, Walmart, DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This way, attackers can get more details about a victim's identity, home address, job and spending habits.

The malware can send stolen data to AI models via the OpenRouter service, which provides access to several AI models.

It first tries to process the collected data using Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.

If the model fails to process the request, VOLTA is hardcoded to try Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

As explained by Cisco Talos, VOLTA specifically looks for refusal responses before attempting to use a different AI model.

It feeds the collected data to the AI models and asks them to analyze it, providing a comprehensive evaluation of a victim's financial worth.

It can also help identify valuable assets and then rank them based on how lucrative they may be. It can also score a victim's cybersecurity.

Essentially, it allows hackers to use AI models to find potentially lucrative targets without the need to manually sift through stolen data.

Binance's 30-day average retail inflows have fallen to just 281 BTC, compared with 2,700 BTC during the 2019–2021 bull cycle.

CryptoQuant identifies spot Bitcoin ETFs as one possible reason behind declining exchange deposits.

Bitcoin is testing support near $77,300, while $78,000 and $76,460 remain key resistance and support levels.

Bitcoin’s retail activity on Binance has fallen to its lowest level in years, even as BTC continues to trade at a much higher valuation than previous market cycles. CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost reports that small-investor inflows have dropped to just 281 BTC.This raises questions about why small investors are no longer showing the same level of activity.

According to analyst Darkfost, Binance’s 30-day average of retail inflows has fallen to just 281 BTC. The metric tracks deposits of less than 1 BTC and shows how much smaller investors are moving onto the exchange.

During the 2019–2021 bull cycle, average retail inflows reached around 2,700 BTC, nearly 10 times the current level. At the time, Bitcoin was trading near $15,700. Activity also picked up in early 2023 after the FTX collapse, when panic pushed average inflows to about 1,900 BTC.

However, the market peaks in March and December 2024 saw much smaller increases, with inflows reaching only 900–1,200 BTC.

The latest figures show a clear gap between Bitcoin’s price and retail activity. BTC is now trading at around $77,414, roughly five times above its bear-market low. Yet retail inflows remain far below previous cycle levels, with the current average around five times lower than the 2020 peak.

Darkfost points to the launch of US spot Bitcoin ETFs in January 2024 as one of the main possible reasons. Before these products entered the market, investors seeking direct Bitcoin exposure often had to purchase BTC through crypto exchanges.

ETFs created another route, allowing investors to gain exposure through traditional investment accounts without managing private wallets.

The scale of this market is already significant as the US spot Bitcoin ETFs have attracted $57.04 billion in cumulative net inflows, while their total net assets reached $102.77 billion as of November 3, 2026.

Another possibility is changing investor behaviour. Some holders may now prefer to keep their Bitcoin for longer rather than frequently deposit or move it between exchanges.

As of now, Bitcoin is down 1.09% to $76,915.34 over the past 24 hours, while the broader crypto market remains mostly flat. The decline has triggered more activity in the derivatives market, with Bitcoin liquidations jumping to $105 million in 24 hours.

Bitcoin is now testing support near $77,300. If this level holds, the price could recover toward resistance at $78,000. However, a clear break below $76,460 could open the way toward the next support near $73,800.

#5224. Crypto Hack Losses Hit $8.74 in 2026, More Than Triple 2025, Yet Without Binance the Year Ran Quieter: How Did Bitcoin and Ethereum React After Major Hacks?

Crypto hack losses hit $8.74B in 2026 vs $2.51B in 2025. Here’s how Bitcoin and Ether moved a day, a week and a month after major hacks.

Crypto hack losses reached $8.74 billion in 2026 by October 31, more than three times the $2.51 billion lost over the same ten months of 2025, after the October 29 Binance breach alone added $6.36 billion.

Take Binance out and the picture flips. The rest of 2026 comes to $2.38 billion, about 5% less than 2025 at the same point, even though attackers hit 325 targets against 120 a year earlier. More attacks, smaller hauls, and then one enormous one.

The market has its own pattern. Across the ten largest hacks since January 2025, Bitcoin’s move on the day of the attack ranged from -4.1% to +1.9%. A month later, for the nine with a full month of data, the range ran from -15.5% to +19.9%, and it followed whatever the broader market was doing.

The 2025 hacks landed in falling markets, and every one was followed by a lower Bitcoin price a month later. Most of 2026’s landed in rising ones.

So how bad has 2026 really been, and what does history say about the weeks after Binance?

The size of the biggest theft. Through September, 2026 was running behind 2025: $2.24 billion lost against $2.48 billion. Then Binance lost $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in one night, more than all of 2025’s hacks put together.

The two years share a culprit. The FBI tied 2025’s largest crypto hack, the $1.4 billion Bybit theft on February 21, to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Chainalysis now ties Binance to the same unit. The biggest hacks of each year:

The rest of 2026 looks different from 2025 too. There were 325 incidents through October, almost three times 2025’s 120, and five 2026 hacks topped $290 million, against one in 2025. Stolen keys and cross-chain bridges did most of the damage outside Binance.

The gross number also overstates what stays lost. CertiK’s October tally counts $3.03 billion frozen or returned, mostly Binance funds caught on-chain, which cuts the month’s adjusted losses to about $3.47 billion. Trackers also disagree on the year: CertiK puts 2026 at $9.2 billion gross and 2025 at $3.35 billion, while DefiLlama has $8.74 billion and $2.72 billion.

DISCOVER: Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying

A small dip on the day, then the market’s own trend. The heatmap compares Bitcoin and Ether with their close the day before each of the ten biggest hacks since 2025.

Bybit is the closest match to Binance: a North Korean exchange theft over $1 billion. Bitcoin lost 14.2% within a week of it, with US tariff fears weighing on markets that week too, and it was still 12.4% lower a month on.

Binance is following a gentler path so far. From the October 28 close to Monday:

Neither yet. Bitcoin trades at $77,870 on Binance, flat on the day, and has held above its October 30 low of $76,326 for three days, right on the 200-day EMA (exponential moving average) at $76,512.

After Bybit, Bitcoin lost its floor within a week. After most of 2026’s hacks, it was higher a month later. The line between the two is clear on the chart: the 200-day EMA below, and the 50-day EMA at $80,293 above.

The crypto hack record says the first day rarely decides much. What Bitcoin does at the 200-day EMA over the next few weeks will show which path this one takes.

#5222. Trezor lifts password ceiling after Coldcard’s $100M wallet thefts

Trezor cited July’s Coldcard attacks, in which strong passphrases helped protect some users whose wallet recovery information was compromised.

Hardware wallet maker Trezor has increased the maximum length of optional wallet passphrases from 50 to 128 characters.

On Sunday, Trezor said the change is available in its Trezor Suite with updated device firmware. Older firmware still limits passphrases to 50 characters.

According to Trezor, a passphrase acts like an additional password that users set alongside their wallet’s recovery phrase. An attacker who obtains the recovery phrase would still need the correct passphrase to access funds in that wallet.

Trezor cited the Coldcard attacks in July, when a firmware flaw caused some devices to generate recovery phrases with insufficient randomness, allowing attackers to reconstruct them. Trezor said strong, unique passphrases protected some affected users.

The update follows a separate warning involving Trezor’s own devices.

On Friday, the company advised customers who bought wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds to new wallets.

An Indonesian customer reported a suspected implant inside a Trezor Safe 5 that could capture on-screen information, including recovery phrases, and transmit it over a cellular network. Trezor said Friday it had not examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.

The compromised hot wallet of the Binance exchange has been completely emptied. Blockchain tracker Whale Alert recorded two identical transactions of 40 million XRP each (around $101 million in total), which went to a new address 50 seconds apart.

This is the platform's corporate address rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. After the October 29 attack, the wallet received an official red "Reported as hacked" label in network explorers.

As a result of this final transfer, the address's balance dropped to 23.7 XRP (around $30) — the exchange fully removed the remaining funds, moving them to new internal wallets.

This transfer effectively closes activity on the vulnerable address and is a planned technical consolidation of the remaining balances. The transfer of assets followed a large-scale cross-chain attack on Binance that began on October 29. Total damage across ten different blockchains is estimated at $6.3 billion, making the incident the largest crypto theft in history.

Hot wallets on the XRP Ledger took the first hit: within five minutes at the start of the attack, a total of 233.46 million XRP (around $296 million) was withdrawn from them.

The specifics of the XRPL network itself oblige the exchange to fully zero out hacked addresses. Unlike most stablecoins (such as USDT or USDC), where issuers can forcibly freeze funds, the XRP Ledger code has no protocol-level blocking function.

Neither Ripple nor independent XRP Ledger developers has no technical ability to stop transactions, so leaving any available balance on a hacked wallet is unsafe. Moving the remaining 80 million XRP to new wallets isolated by the platform eliminates the risk of repeated withdrawals.

For the XRP ecosystem, this incident became an absolute all-time negative record, surpassing the September hack of the Bitget exchange, in which 103 million XRP ($157 million) was lost, multiple times over.

At the same time, no panic has been recorded on the market. Binance has fully restored withdrawal operations for clients. The platform's management officially stated that all net user losses will be compensated 1:1 from corporate reserves and SAFU fund money.

The transfer of the last $101 million in XRP likely puts an end to operations with the hacked address, minimizing further technical risks for the platform.

In Bitcoin news on Tuesday, November 3, North Korea rejected US claims that its hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, as Kim Yo Jong called the FBI’s attribution “absurd rhetoric” and suggested that Washington itself might be behind the heist.

The statement, carried by the state news agency KCNA, came three days after the FBI named TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit, as the culprit.

It changes little on the ground. Blockchain firms Chainalysis, TRM Labs and Elliptic had already tied the theft to North Korea, and the money is still moving.

That is why it matters for Bitcoin. Elliptic counts $3.24 billion still sitting in wallets linked to the attackers, mostly in Bitcoin and Ether, and it saw the first stolen BTC go through a mixer on Monday.

BTC slipped 1.8% to $76,729 on the day, back on its 200-day average, and the Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 37 to 26.

So what exactly did North Korea say, and how much of the stolen money could still hit the market?

New account creation on the XRP Ledger jumped 142.4%, according to XRPScan data. It points to renewed interest in the ecosystem, even though XRP is still struggling to get its bullish momentum back.

XRPScan counted 7,734 newly activated accounts on November 1, 2026, up 33% from the day before and far above the network's 30-day average of roughly 3,500 new accounts a day.

Wallet creation is clearly speeding up. What's behind it is still unclear.

There are a few plausible explanations. Interest in tokenized assets, stablecoins, and decentralized finance apps on the XRPL may be pushing people to set up new wallets. Exchange onboarding and automated wallet creation could also be adding to the count.

But more accounts doesn't necessarily mean more users. One person can open several accounts, and automated systems can open many more, so other on-chain indicators are needed to judge real adoption.

XRPScan's history also shows account creation has spiked before, with an all-time high of about 30,600 accounts. The latest jump is well short of that.

The network numbers are growing, but the price paints a different picture.

TradingView data from November 2 shows XRP trading near $1.25, after a long correction from its September and October highs. It is still below several major moving averages, so bearish pressure continues to dominate the technical picture.

Immediate support sits around $1.20–$1.25. If XRP tries to recover, the $1.30-$1.35 region could act as resistance.

Rising account creation alongside falling prices reflects blockchain adoption and market demand, which are not the same thing. Stronger confirmation of growing XRPL adoption would need sustained growth in active addresses, transaction volumes, and general use of the ecosystem.

For now, the 142.4% increase is an encouraging sign of network activity. Whether it turns into real demand for XRP is still an open question.

#5215. Ripple and Water.org Expand Stablecoin Work as Aid Payments Move Faster

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Ripple and Water.org are expanding a partnership that applies payment and stablecoin infrastructure to water and sanitation financing. Ripple’s late-October announcement describes wider use of Ripple Payments, RLUSD and wallet services across the nonprofit’s operations.

The company reports that earlier work moved more than $3.2 million across four markets, with same-day settlement in Mexico and Brazil replacing waits of two to three days. Those are partner-reported operational results, not an independent measure of every programme outcome.

Water.org’s WaterCredit programme works with local financial institutions to make small loans for household water and sanitation improvements. Its role includes supporting partners with resources and expertise, while those institutions provide the financing.

That model makes the movement of capital an important operational link. Money may originate in one country, pass through an international funding arrangement and ultimately support a local loan used to install a tap, toilet or other improvement.

Speed in one part of that chain can help, particularly when it reduces idle balances or uncertainty over when funds will arrive. It cannot substitute for sound lending, reliable local contractors or a household’s ability to use the completed infrastructure.

A cross-border transfer can involve several forms of cost: bank charges, currency conversion, the time staff spend reconciling records and the cash held while a payment is pending. A change in infrastructure may improve some of those elements without changing all of them.

The useful comparison is therefore the amount and timing of usable money at the destination. A token arriving quickly is not the same as a local lender having the currency and information needed to disburse a loan.

For example, a settlement message that arrives over a weekend may still require a local conversion or approval process. Measuring that whole sequence would show whether continuous digital settlement translates into a practical advantage for the programme.

Adding a stablecoin gives an organization another way to hold and transfer a claim denominated in dollars. It also creates tasks around access permissions, reconciliation and the conditions for converting the balance into another form of money.

A nonprofit’s finance team needs to connect those balances to grants, programme budgets and expenditure records. The technology is most useful when it fits that discipline, rather than requiring the organization to maintain a separate set of unexplained onchain transactions.

Custody and wallet services can form part of that operating model. The important question is who is allowed to move funds and how the organization checks that an instruction matches an approved purpose. Faster settlement increases the value of getting those controls right before execution.

Payment completion times and processing costs show whether the financial infrastructure works more efficiently. Household access to safe water and sanitation shows whether the wider programme achieves its purpose. Both are relevant, but one should not be used as an automatic proxy for the other.

A credible expansion would report the relationship between the two: whether lower costs leave more funding available, whether quicker transfers improve loan availability and whether local delivery remains reliable as the programme grows.

For crypto, this is an adoption story with a concrete use for moving money, rather than a claim that a token’s price must benefit. The partnership gives Ripple and Water.org a setting in which payment infrastructure can be assessed against a practical objective. The strongest results will be those that trace an operational improvement through to the people the financing is intended to reach.

#5213. SAT Japan Adds USDT and USDC Payments With Dollar Settlement Through Triple-A

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Japanese vehicle exporter SAT Japan has added a stablecoin payment route through Triple-A, targeting the cross-border transfers involved in buying a car from overseas. The October 29 announcement says eligible customers can use USDT and USDC while the exporter receives settlement in US dollars.

The arrangement puts the payment processor between the buyer’s digital asset and the seller’s preferred currency. SAT Japan does not need to hold or manage the stablecoins itself, according to the companies.

A vehicle purchase involves more than clicking a checkout button. The seller needs to connect a substantial incoming payment to a specific vehicle and buyer, while the customer wants confidence that the transfer has arrived before shipping arrangements proceed.

Cross-border banking can add uncertainty about fees, intermediary deductions and processing times. A stablecoin route offers a different way to move value, but its commercial usefulness depends on the clarity of the complete transaction.

The buyer needs to know which asset and network are accepted, how long a quoted amount remains valid and when the seller will treat the invoice as paid. A transfer that reaches the wrong address or uses an unsupported network is not rescued by the fact that the token is designed to track a dollar.

Receiving dollars allows the exporter to separate customer payment choice from the currency it uses for accounting and operations. That is a different proposition from a business deciding to accumulate cryptocurrency on its balance sheet.

The processor’s role is central to that separation. It must recognize the payment, carry out the required checks and deliver the agreed settlement. The blockchain leg can be rapid while the overall process still includes compliance and banking steps.

This makes the service closer to an alternative payment rail than a bet on token prices. The seller’s objective is to receive a usable, reconciled payment for a vehicle. The buyer’s objective is to complete the purchase using money they can access.

Changing the payment method does not establish the condition of a vehicle, its shipping timetable or whether it meets the rules in the destination country. Those remain parts of the purchase agreement and import process.

A payment confirmation can prove that funds moved, but it cannot by itself prove that the promised goods were delivered. Buyers and sellers still need clear documentation identifying the vehicle, the agreed price and the responsibilities around transport and cancellation.

Refund handling is another practical question. If a purchase cannot proceed, the parties need to know whether a refund will be made in bank money or a digital asset, how any conversion is priced and who bears the associated charges. Those details should be understandable before a high-value transfer is sent.

The most revealing metrics would be the number of customers choosing the new option, the time to confirmed settlement and the total cost compared with the alternatives available to those same buyers.

Geography will matter. A method that improves a particular corridor may offer little advantage where bank transfers are already cheap and predictable. Eligibility and local access also determine whether the option is genuinely convenient for an overseas customer.

SAT Japan and Triple-A have identified a plausible use case for stablecoins: moving substantial payments across borders while allowing a conventional merchant to settle in a familiar currency. The test is whether the integration reduces uncertainty in actual purchases, including exceptions and refunds, rather than simply adding another logo to the payment page.

#5212. Big Week Ahead as XRP Ledger Eyes Cleanup Upgrade

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is set for a significant week ahead as its long-awaited cleanup upgrade heads for mainnet activation this week, bringing a wide-ranging collection of fixes and improvements to the blockchain.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment, a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation, is at the center of attention, with validator support putting it on track for a potential November 4 activation, provided the required voting threshold of 80% is sustained.

The earliest activation date is Nov 4, 2026 at 2:46 PM UTC, with just 2 days left according to the xrpscan countdown timer.

Some tokens on the XRP Ledger are supposed to be stored in accounts approved by their issuer; however, developers have found a few ways around that rule.

Issuers of regulated assets, such as stablecoins or tokenized funds, can require approval before anyone holds their tokens, typically to perform identity checks first.

Four proposed code changes would resolve the remaining exceptions. All four are included in a single network upgrade dubbed fixCleanup3_5_0.

These have not been merged into the XRP Ledger's main software yet. Once they are, fixCleanup3_5_0 requires support from more than 80% of the network's trusted validators for two weeks before being activated.

According to Hussein Zangana (Vet), director of community at XRP Ledger Foundation, there is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability on kernels 4.4+, affecting any unpatched Linux server in the world with an open IPv4 TCP port. For XRP Ledger node and validator operators who run RHEL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK, a fix has already been shipped; they are simply expected to update and reboot.

For those who run Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, this might not suffice, as they may need to take further steps until a fix is shipped for their distro. They should re-apply the nft rule after a reboot or a flush ruleset reload.
